title: HIGH POWER OPTICAL TERMINATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a high power optical termination for polarisation maintaining fibers.DescriptionOptical feeder-links to and from future terabit telecommunication satellites will require high powertransmit beams. The continuous development of optical amplifiers for space applications has demonstrated optical power of 10 Watts and next generation is targetting 100 Watts. This opens the question on the definition of the optical interface between the fibered optical amplifier and the beam in free space that would minimise the risk of catastrophic optical damage to the fiber end.The currently available space qualified connector is not designed to cope with several Watts. To help with the high power, this activity aims at developing a fiber termini or a connector in order to provide the thermal management of the high power, a robust mechanical interface to the focal plane and deliver a high quality optical beam.Typical reliability requirements are based on GEO type application for 15 to 18 years, radiationhardened, 500 thermal cycling resistant and capable to operate in vacuum. The type of the output fiber is expected to be a polarisation maintaining at 1550 nm,and the cable assembly is to be testedagainst thermal cycling and humidity, mechanical environments and radiation resistance as aminimum.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Establish requirements specification based on focal plane suppliers- Design and materials selection- Prototype of the high power termination, draft of the product identification document and thetest plan- Environmental testing (thermal cycling, humidity, mechanical environments, and radiations)- Draft detail specifications.

Tietomallintamisen tarkkuus on esitetty tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa. Tietomallin lähtötietoina rakennuttaja teettää fotogrammetriset mittaukset rakennuksen julkisivuista, vesikatoista ja tontista sekä pistepilvet rakennuksen yleisistä tiloista ja tyyppiasunnoista. Hankkeen Urakkakilpailu suoritetaan kilpailullisena neuvottelumenettelynä, missä suunnitelmavaiheessa pyydetään kriteerit täyttäviltä noin viideltä urakoitsijalta kommentit suunnitelmiin osana urakkakilpailua. Kommenttien perusteella karsitaan tarjoajat 3-5 tarjoajaan. Suunnitteluryhmän tulee osallistua urakkalaskentavaiheessa urakoitsijoilta tulleiden kehitysehdotusten läpikäyntiin yhdessä rakennuttajan kanssa. Lisäksi suunnitteluryhmän tulee osallistua työpajoihin rakennuttajan ja urakoitsijan kanssa. Työpajojen kestoksi on arvioitu yhteensä noin 25 tuntia. Suunnittelijoiden tulee päivittää suunnitelmia valittujen kehitysehdotusten mukaisesti. Lopullinen urakkatarjouspyyntö laaditaan päivitetyillä suunnitelmilla kolmelle tarjoajalle. Suunnitteluhankinta sisältää Rakentamislain mukaiset velvollisuudet sekä rakentamislain rakentamisluvan mukaiset viranomaisvelvoitteet ja vaatimukset mukaan lukien tietomallivaateet niin lupa- kuin vastaanottovaiheessa kaikkien suunnittelualojen osalta. Poikkeamispäätöksen ja sijoitusluvan/sijoitussopimuksen hakeminen kuuluvat suunnittelutehtävään, jos sellaisia tarvitaan. Peruskorjauksen kohteena on Helsingin kaupungin asunnot Oy:n omistama vuokratalokohde, joka sijaitsee Helsingin kaupungin tontilla 22556/5 (Anjalantie 2, Sammatintie 10 ja Sammatintie 12, 00550 Helsinki). Hankkeeseen kuuluu myös piha-alue tontilla 22556/4, joka on yhteiskäytössä Kangasalantie 13 kanssa. Hankintaa ei jaeta osiin, sillä usean toimittajan malli tuottaisi epätarkoituksenmukaisen sopimuskokonaisuuden aikataulunhallinnan sekä töiden yhteensovittamisen kannalta. title: TIME DIVISION DUPLEXING (TDD) KA-BAND IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT FOR NGSO 5G BROADBAND SERVICES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3E.029)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and perform an in-orbit experiment of Non-GeoSynchornous Orbit (NGSO) payload technology to prove the feasibility of Time Division Duplexing method in Ka-band for broadband services, allowing operators to gain access to 3 GHz of additional Ka-band spectrum (24.5 - 27.5 GHz) via 5G New Radio waveform in Frequency Range 2 (FR2).Targeted Improvements:Access to an additional 3 GHz of terrestrial spectrum between 24.5-27.5GHz. 30% improvement in spectrum efficiency due to Time Division Duplexing optimisation.Description: The use of Time Domain Duplexing (TDD) for satellite communications can provide access to an additional 3 GHz of Ka-band spectrum (24.5 - 27.5 GHz) via 5G New Radio waveform in Frequency Range 2 (FR 2). The feasibility of employing this technology in Non-Geosynchronous Orbit (NGSO) broadband systems depends on the round-trip time as well as on the waveform and system operations (e.g., synchronisation), which necessitate in-orbit tests to confirm feasibility. TDD technology is highly latency dependent, and there exists a number of technical challenges to be addressed in-orbit:- ability to synchronise uplink with downlink on the satellite payload as well as the user terminal- varying guard times that are required under various geometrical configurations- timing reference accuracy required by the payload- frequency of ephemeris update rate required at the terminal- RF front-end performance given the Tx/Rx co-existence- ability of the ground segment to schedule various uplink/downlink capacity allocations (from e.g. 90/10 down- to up-link ratio to 50/50 down- to up-link ratio). The activity shall therefore develop a scaled Ka-band payload engineering model, employing the 5G New Radio waveform and shall confirm the feasibility of TDD in Ka-band systems in real operating conditions by testing the payload in-orbit. The payload shall be embarked on a NGSO hosted payload service, for a period of at least 4 months, in order to test it under a variety of operating conditions (e.g., different elevations) and 5G New Radio waveform configurations (e.g., different guard time intervals). The activity shall implement all necessary elements for performing the in-orbit experimental mission, such as: - Licensing (e.g. under Article 4.4 of the ITU-R Radio Regulations) - Contracting a hosted payload service and mission operations - Ground segment provision.The activity shall be implemented in a phased approach, to ensure alignment with the latest 3GPP updates. title: Request for information: Large gene panel for analysis of somatic genetic alterations in cancer
description: HUSLAB is seeking a large gene panel test for detection of genetic alterations in cancer covering genes with the most common clinically relevant alterations (at least 500 genes). The test should detect SNVs, indels, gene fusions, copy number variations (CNVs), microsatellite instability (MSI), homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), and tumor mutation burden (TMB). The test is based on analysis of total nucleic acids (RNA and DNA) extracted from paraffin embedded solid tumor samples using next generation sequencing (NGS) on either Ion Torrent or NovaSeq 6000 sequencers. The number of cancer panel tests annually in HUSLAB is estimated to be between 500-1000. This is not a call for tenders and we are not asking for any offers via this announcement. This prior information notice does not obligate the procurement unit for any actions. All information presented in this prior information notice is preliminary and indicative. This notice is not binding on any kind of solutions or actions. The suppliers are not paid for responding to this request for information or participating in a possible technical dialogue. HUSLAB Laboratory of Genetics at HUS (Helsinki University Hospital) Diagnostic Center is an SFS-EN ISO 15189:2013 accredited laboratory providing diagnostic genetic testing services to all patients at Helsinki University Hospital area. The services include analysis of both constitutional samples and malignancies. The laboratory provides sequencing services mainly using local HUSLAB sequencing capacity (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, Ion Torrent S5 and Ion Torrent Proton equipment). We ask companies interested in this procurement to answer the following questions and requests listed below: - The test is validated for Ion Torrent equipment. (Yes/No) - The test is validated for Illumina NovaSeq 6000. (Yes/No) - The test is validated for paraffin embedded samples. (Yes/No) - The automatic extraction methods used in the laboratory (Maxwell, QIAsymphony) are suitable for test. (Yes/No) - Provide a list of laboratory equipment needed to perform the test. - The number of genes covered by the panel is over 500. (Yes/No) - Provide a list of genes covered by the panel, specifying which genes are covered completely or partially and in the latter case, information on which parts of the genes are covered. Furthermore, the list should specify for which genes can CNVs and fusions be detected. - Novel fusion partners are identified. (Yes/No) - The cancer panel covers the most common exon skipping (at least MET exon 14) in solid tumors. (Yes/No) - MSI, TMB, and HRD are reported. (Yes/No) - Allele frequency, depth, breakpoints and sequence of variants are reported. (Yes/No) - SNVs and indels can be detected in the same sequencing run as fusion genes. (Yes/No) - What is the limit of detection (LOD)? - How many samples can be run in one chip/flow cell? - The test includes a tertiary data analysis software. (Yes/No) - Is the test CE-IVDR certified? (Yes/No) - If No, how does the manufacturer plan to acquire IVDR certification for the test? The response to this request for information should include replies to the above questions. The answers to this request for information are asked to be sent by e-mail to kilpailutus.laboratorio@hus.fi. We wish to receive a response to our request at the latest on August 15th 2023.
